requirements.evidence: All contract points covered: migrations for totems/totem_presets/totem_preset_queue with composite PK (create_totem_preset_queue_table.php:15-19); `totem:pairing-code {preset}` with random_int + zero-pad, 10 min expiry, consumed reset, audit log, non-zero exit on unknown id (OpenTotemPairing.php:18-46, PairingCode.php:17-24); POST /api/totem/auth with 400/401/200 + entity pair, lockForUpdate transaction (PairTotem.php:28-73, TotemAuthController.php:17-40); HS256 claims totem_id/entity_id/preset_id/queues/iat/exp/jti from services.totem.* (TotemToken.php:20-33, config/services.php:38-41, phpunit.xml:44-45, .env.example); middleware 401 cases and claim ∩ current join scope (AuthenticateTotem.php:31-53); 403 forbidden/404 queue_not_found/422 inactive_queue/invalid_priority, visual.order, backend-owned TicketPriority enum, IssueTicket with TicketChannel::Totem (TotemQueueController.php:27-136); throttles 10/30 + JSON rate_limited on api/* (AppServiceProvider.php:28-30, bootstrap/app.php:27-31); CORS pattern + TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN, no credentials (config/cors.php); docs updated from proposal to implemented; entity_suspended documented as reserved.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through Actions (OpenTotemPairing, PairTotem, reuse of IssueTicket); Fillable attributes set deliberately with login_code* excluded (TotemPreset.php:12-13); reversible migrations with generator-style timestamps; docs (api/totem.md, database-schema.md, architecture.md, business-rules.md, CHANGELOG, devops.md) kept in sync. Deviations: HTTP input is validated by hand (`preg_match` in TotemAuthController.php:19, `filter_var` in TotemQueueController.php:83-86) rather than `$request->validate`/Form Request, defensible given the custom error bodies; the architecture.md paragraph was merged into one very long line.

security.evidence: JWT verification checks the signature in constant time before parsing, pins alg HS256, type-checks claims and exp, and fails closed on a secret under 32 chars (TotemToken.php:53-90, 108-115). Middleware re-checks totem/preset active and entity consistency on every call; path slugs are never trusted: the queue is resolved within the token entity (TotemQueueController.php:107-138). Pairing gives the same 401 for every failure reason with no oracle, the code is never logged (TotemAuthController.php:43-49), consume happens under a row lock, and pairing is throttled. CORS uses an anchored regex (`\A...\z`). Minor robustness point: strict `!==` comparison of an uncast `entity_id` attribute against int claims (AuthenticateTotem.php:38-39) depends on the PDO driver returning ints, but it fails closed.

tests.evidence: Six Pest files cover models/factories/cascades (TotemModelsTest), the command including unknown id, replacement, uniqueness and audit-without-code (TotemPairingCodeCommandTest), auth format/oracle/consumed/throttle/TTL/audit (TotemAuthTest), the JWT codec with alg none/HS512/tamper/wrong secret/type checks (TotemTokenTest), every middleware 401 case, scope intersection, 403/404/422 paths, invalid-priority datasets with no ticket created, sequential codes and the 30/min throttle (TotemEndpointsTest), and CORS allow/deny including lookalike origins (TotemCorsTest). Only the concurrent-pairing race is untested. `RateLimiter::clear('totem-auth')` does not clear the real per-IP key, but it is harmless.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses IssueTicket and the existing InactiveQueueException; the TicketPriority enum is the single source for both endpoints. The JWT implementation is small and the task allows it. Small redundancies: the InactiveQueueException catch (TotemQueueController.php:94-96) duplicates the is_active check already done in issuableQueue; the `?: $request->ip()` fallback in AppServiceProvider.php:30 is dead code because sha1() never returns an empty string; `->values()` after `get()` is a no-op (TotemQueueController.php:38).

readability.evidence: Small, focused classes with PHPDoc that explains intent (e.g. the 'row lock' comment in PairTotem.php:29 and the 'Fail closed' comment in TotemToken.php:112). Error rendering is centralised in TotemApiException::render. Names are clear (issuableQueue, tokenEntity, invalidToken). Style matches sibling files (Fillable attribute, casts() method).

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task. The extra docs touches (docs/README.md, business-rules.md, ops/devops.md secret row, CHANGELOG) follow the docs-in-sync convention. No operator UI, refresh tokens or billing were added.

issues.explanation: Input is validated by hand instead of with `$request->validate`/a Form Request; this is justified by the custom `{code}` error bodies but departs from the stated controller validation pattern.

Strict `!==` between the uncast `entity_id` model attribute and the int claim relies on the DB driver returning ints; if it returns a string, every valid token would be rejected (fails closed, but brittle).
`sha1(...) ?: $request->ip()` never falls back because sha1 always returns a non-empty string.
The InactiveQueueException catch repeats the is_active check already done in issuableQueue (it only helps under a race).
`RateLimiter::clear('totem-auth')` does not clear the actual limiter key (name+IP hash), so the call is a no-op.
The edited paragraph was joined into one very long line, which breaks the surrounding line wrapping.

review.summary: The change implements the totem BFF end to end: migrations, models, factories, the pairing command, the JWT auth endpoint, the `totem.auth` middleware with scope intersection, the three data endpoints reusing IssueTicket, throttles, CORS and updated docs. It is backed by thorough Pest tests covering failure, authorization and tamper paths. Only minor issues remain (hand-rolled input validation, a strict uncast id comparison, small redundancies), so I would approve with nits.
